Materials and Reagents Biological materials Twelve-day-old Arabidopsis thaliana ecotype Columbia (Col_0) seedlings Solutions DEPC-treated water Milli-Q water treated with 0.2% (v/v) DEPC for 24 h at room temperature and autoclaved for 20 min in a glass bottle. Cool down the bottled water at room temperature for 24 h before use. (Can be stored indefinitely if the bottle is unopened) All reagent stocks (except sucrose solution, cycloheximide, RNase inhibitor and DTT) should be made in a glass beaker and stored in a 100 mL glass bottle in the dark at room temperature. (Replace with new stock after three months) Cycloheximide (CHX, 50 mg/mL) stock is made by resuspending 50 mg of cycloheximide in 1 mL of ethanol in a 1.5 mL tube. Store stock solution at -20 °C. (Replace with new stock after three months) Chloramphenicol (CHL, 50 mg/mL) stock is made by resuspending 50 mg of chloramphenicol in 1 mL of ethanol in a 1.5 mL tube. Store stock solution at -20 °C. (Replace with new stock after three months) Dithiothreitol (DTT, 1 M) stock is made by resuspending 0.154 g of DTT in 1 mL of water in a 1.5 mL tube. Store stock solution at -20 °C. (Replace with new stock after two months) Sucrose solutions made in a glass beaker need to be filtered through a 0.2 µm PVDF filter bottle and stored in the dark at 4 °C. (Replace with new stock after one month. Before each use, always shake the bottle to check for any cloudy appearance. Discard and make new solutions as necessary) Punch solution should be made in a glass bottle and autoclaved for 20 min on liquid cycle. (Can be stored indefinitely at room temperature in the dark) 100 mL of 1 M Tris-HCl (pH 8.4) is made by dissolving 12.14 g of Tris in 80 mL of deionized water and adjusting the pH to 8.4 using 0.1 N HCl. After attaining the desired pH, the volume of 1 M Tris-HCl solution is adjusted to final 100 mL using deionized water. steps.title: Grow and freeze Arabidopsis seedlings
steps.instruction: Germinate Columbia (Col‑0) Arabidopsis seeds on ½× MS medium, grow for 12 days, harvest seedlings into 1.5 mL tubes, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C (use within 1–2 months).

steps.title: Decontaminate gloves with RNaseZap
steps.instruction: Apply RNaseZap™ decontamination solution to gloves before any further manipulation.

steps.title: Clean gradient maker (day before)
steps.instruction: One day prior, rinse the gradient maker with diluted dish‑soap in warm tap water for 1–2 min, then rinse with warm tap water a few minutes; clean the micro‑stirrer bar with warm water and dry with wipes; rinse the gradient maker twice with DEPC‑treated water and air‑dry on wipes.

steps.title: Arrange bench and set up gradient maker
steps.instruction: Place pipettes, tips, burette stand, magnetic stirrer plate, micro‑stirrer bar, 2.2 mL polypropylene tubes, 1.5 mL tube rack, waste containers and stock solutions (15 % & 50 % sucrose, CHX, CHL, DTT) on a stable bench. Attach the gradient‑maker support rod to the burette‑stand holder and adjust its height so the base of the maker is ~0.5–1 in above the stirrer plate. Insert the micro‑stirrer bar into the chamber connected to the outlet tubing (Well‑II) and turn the stirrer on to confirm rotation. Turn the push‑pull valve to face “self” (closed between Well‑I and Well‑II). Clamp a binder clip 1 in from the outlet valve and attach a 10 µL pipette tip (broad side to tubing, tip side for elution).

steps.title: Prepare CHX‑CHL‑DTT mix
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL tube add 15 µL cycloheximide stock (50 mg mL⁻¹), 15 µL chloramphenicol stock (50 mg mL⁻¹) and 1.5 µL DTT stock (1 M); vortex 10–20 s at room temperature and keep on ice.

steps.title: Assemble sucrose gradient (pre‑run)
steps.instruction: For each gradient: (a) add 2.1 µL of the CHL‑CHX‑DTT mix along the side wall of both Well‑I and Well‑II; (b) add 1 mL 15 % sucrose to Well‑I and 1 mL 50 % sucrose to Well‑II while the stirrer rotates in Well‑II; (c) gently remove the binder clamp to allow ~1 cm of 50 % sucrose to flow into the outlet tubing (optionally control flow with a 200 µL tip attached to a 20–200 µL pipette), then reclamp; (d) turn the push‑pull valve to the horizontal position (open conduit between wells); (e) release trapped air by sealing the top of Well‑I with a gloved finger and pressing down slightly; (f) place the outlet tubing tip into the bottom of a 2.2 mL ultracentrifuge tube, ensure the outlet is level with the bottom of Well‑II, open the clamp and let the solutions flow by gravity, draining evenly from both wells; (g) when ~200 µL remains in Well‑II, tilt the gradient maker clockwise until its base contacts the stirrer plate and the outlet tip touches the top of the formed gradient, allowing the remaining liquid to exit; (h) place the finished gradient tube in a 1.5 mL tube rack and cover with aluminum foil; (i) repeat steps (a)–(h) for all required gradients; (j) adjust each gradient tube to a total weight of 2.800 g by adding a small amount of 15 % sucrose solution on top.

steps.title: Pre‑run gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Place each gradient tube (in a 1.5 mL rack) into a TLS‑55 rotor bucket pre‑chilled at 4 °C, matching the weight of all four buckets using 15 % sucrose solution; spin at 50,000 rpm (213 626 × g) for 70 min at 4 °C with deceleration = 0 (no brake). After the run, return tubes to the rack, cover with foil and store at 4 °C without shaking (pre‑run gradients remain usable for up to 24 h).

steps.title: Prepare mortar‑pestle and grind tissue
steps.instruction: Two days before, wash mortars and pestles with dish‑soap, rinse with tap water, autoclave 30 min (dry setting), then store at –20 °C (or –80 °C) overnight. On the day of the experiment, add liquid nitrogen to the cold mortar‑pestle until boiling stops. Keep frozen seedling tissue from –80 °C storage floating in a dewar of liquid nitrogen, transfer to the mortar and grind to a fine powder for 4–5 min, adding liquid nitrogen every minute to keep the material cold. Weigh 150 mg of powder into a pre‑chilled 1.5 mL tube using a pre‑chilled spatula; keep the tube with an open cap in a Styrofoam container with liquid nitrogen while waiting.

steps.title: Lyse tissue and clarify extract
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL freshly prepared lysis buffer (final concentrations: 200 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.4, 50 mM KCl, 25 mM MgCl₂, 1 % deoxycholic acid, 2 % polyoxyethylene 10 tridecyl ether, 50 µg mL⁻¹ cycloheximide, 40 U mL⁻¹ RNase inhibitor) to the tube, incubate 40–50 s at room temperature, close the cap and vortex at highest speed for 1 min at RT; repeat vortexing once more for complete homogenisation. Centrifuge at 21 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, transfer 125 µL supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube, and repeat centrifugation under the same conditions.

steps.title: Load sample onto sucrose gradient
steps.instruction: Carefully layer 100 µL of the clarified supernatant onto a pre‑made 15 %–50 % sucrose gradient (or, for a blank, layer 100 µL lysis buffer). Number tubes if desired.

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge sample gradients
steps.instruction: Place each loaded gradient tube into a TLS‑55 rotor bucket chilled at 4 °C, match the weight of all buckets using 15 % sucrose solution, and spin at 50 000 rpm (213 626 × g) for 70 min at 4 °C with deceleration = 0. After centrifugation, remove tubes, place in a 1.5 mL rack, cover with foil and keep on ice.

steps.title: Set up fractionator and run punch solution
steps.instruction: Clamp the gradient tube in the gradient fractionator and seal it against the top assembly. Load a 2.2 mL tube containing punch solution (100 % sucrose, 0.02 % bromophenol blue, 1 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.4) wrapped with a 2 cm wide piece of parafilm for grip. Run the punch solution at the lowest pump speed (≈ 375 µL min⁻¹) until it emerges from the piercing needle, establishing a baseline (A₂₅₄ nm ≈ 0) at sensitivity 0.5.

steps.title: Record blank and collect fractions
steps.instruction: After the water run, remove the tube and load the blank gradient tube; record the blank absorbance. Wash the fractionator tubing with 50 mL warm water, dry inlet and outlet with wipes, and apply vacuum; verify baseline returns to zero. Load the first sample gradient tube, then collect eight 200 µL fractions into individual 1.5 mL tubes, placing each tube on ice immediately. After each gradient run repeat the tubing‑wash procedure before the next sample.
